propositions.claim: Lead only. The Library of Congress OCR text of Lord (1943) p. 175 (image 197), re-fetched 2026-11-18 through a summarising fetch, contains an entry referring to the Executive Order of May 17, 1899 establishing the Fort Lincoln ('Lancoln' in the OCR) Military Reservation, N. Dak., followed by citations to the 1907, 1910 and 1916 'MR' volumes and to GLO references. The OCR is noisy, the line breaks below are the OCR's, and the page image was not read. The word 'amended' given in the earlier quotation and the date Aug. 31, 1899 did not appear in the re-fetched text, so neither is asserted from this source.

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN and formal status unknown are appropriate on the confirmed evidence. A table description cannot establish the complete operative clauses or satisfy the rule requiring the order's own sentence for spent-on-issue treatment. No accepted original text or current-operation evidence was established. T1 is therefore unmet, and the cumulative tier remains T0.
missed_evidence: The cited CFR PDF, printed p. 330, footnote 1 says 'Appears in tabulated form.' This resolves the footnote-meaning portion of gap 3; it establishes neither current operation nor an ending.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (BUDGET fits the documented unfinished original-text search better than NOT_FOUND: specific compilation-page leads remain listed without evidence of inspection or exhaustion; the evidence slice supplies identification, not proof that the original cannot be found)

verdicts.reason: The cited Lord OCR endpoint and alternative representation of the same catalogue page were inaccessible. Neither the quotation nor the MR/GLO references could be independently confirmed.
The cited CFR PDF, printed p. 222, confirms the partial-revocation description, August 31, 1899 date, blank order number, and reference to 10 CFR 51.1(a), footnote 1.
The same page confirms the May 17, 1899 military-land reservation entry, blank order number, and 10 CFR 51.1(a) reference.
The same page confirms the June 8, 1901 Fort Lincoln addition entry. Its description does not identify either 1899 order; treating it only as candidate context is appropriate.
